content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm new here. As a Mechanical Engineering student, I'm currently working on updating an old refrigeration test bench at my university. The bank needs repairs and I plan to replace analog indicators with digital devices. I found [product_name] online and thought it might fit my requirements. I need to continuously monitor five pressure points and five temperature points on a PC using software (I considered Labview, but [product_name] seems to have its own software that might be simpler). This setup would allow students to perform heat transfer experiments and other thermodynamics demonstrations. I'd appreciate your input and any advice or ideas on tackling this project. Thanks! (A photo of the test bench is attached.)
No, this isn't possible with [product_name]. It supports a maximum of 8 analog inputs, but you need 10. Your refrigeration system is quite old.

Thank you for sharing your thoughts. I believed that [product_name] offered expansion modules to increase the number of analog inputs. Am I mistaken? This test bank was built in 1992 and was taken out of service in 1997, but now the university wants a restoration.
You are correct: extension modules can increase analog inputs, but the maximum limit remains 8 analog inputs for a single [product_name] base module.

Understood, thanks for clarifying. Now I see I'll need two [product_name] units for the test bank. Would having two modules connected to the PC using [product_name] software cause any conflicts? Has anyone tried running multiple devices in a single process before? I'm also researching what modules are required for temperature readings (specifically [product_name] analog modules). Do I need a separate module for each temperature sensing point? Sorry for all my questions—I'm a bit lost, but your help is greatly appreciated. Best regards

If you're using two [product_name] units, each will need its own program, which means programming the first for some sensors and the second for the rest. Each [product_name] operates independently. The [product_name] analog input module can measure certain voltage and current outputs. If your sensors are PT100 or PT1000 types, you need a corresponding module designed for them. Each analog module typically provides two analog inputs.

I see. So, both programs could run simultaneously to display all measured points together. If I buy one [product_name] base, I’d get 4 analog inputs—and with two analog extension modules, the total would be 8. That's enough for 4 pressure readings and 4 temperature measurements. Is this correct? If so, I'd actually need 3 analog modules and two base units, which could become quite costly. Is there a more affordable alternative?

Correct. One [product_name] base module offers 4 analog inputs, and adding two specific modules provides additional analog inputs for PT100 or PT1000 sensors. If you need more than this, a second [product_name] base and extra modules are necessary. I'm not familiar with the pricing of these modules.

Thank you for your support. Your explanations have helped me understand the challenges. I'm checking prices locally and it looks like choosing [product_name] could increase my project costs. Do you know if there are alternative solutions from [company_name] for this setup? Best regards
I suggest contacting a local [company_name] sales partner for assistance. You can find contact details at [url].

analysis.insight_summary: The user is seeking options to modernize an old refrigeration test bench, focusing on replacing analog measurements with digital ones that can be monitored via PC. During review, they identified that a single [product_name] setup does not support the necessary number of analog inputs and are unclear about expansion capabilities, module choices, and integration with PC interfaces. Concerns include system complexity and increased costs if multiple modules are needed.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking for a simple, expandable system using [product_name] hardware and software to handle at least ten analog sensor inputs and allow easy PC connectivity for real-time monitoring. They hope for cost-effective recommendations and practical advice from experienced users, expecting modular solutions and clear configuration guidance.
